text: A column shuffle writes the message in rows under a key and reads the columns in the key's alphabetical order. Done twice, with one key seven letters long, it is the double transposition nobody had run with a 7.
After both shuffles, a repeating secret word on the table must give the copper's letters where the known letters landed; two known letters in one slot of the word must agree.
All 5,040 orders of seven columns with 253 second shuffles, either first: no word of 1 to 20 letters fits, and 21-26 fit as often as on scrambled coppers.
